correctness.rationale: Taking the common line and one perpendicular unit direction in each disk plane gives an invertible image of the orthogonal model for all positive smaller plane angles, including the right angle. Covariance and squared volume both acquire the squared determinant in their quotient. Orthogonal fibres are exactly [-f-g,f+g], where f=sqrt(a^2-y^2), g=sqrt(b^2-z^2). Symmetry centers the distribution and kills cross terms. Integrating gives V=2πab(a+b), raw x moment π(a^4 b+a b^4)/2+4π(a^3 b^2+a^2 b^3)/3, and raw y moment πa^4 b/2+2πa^3 b^2/3 (swap a,b for z). These follow respectively from (2/3)(f+g)^3 and 2y^2(f+g); division by V produces the recorded covariance. In the determinant quotient, (3a+4b)(4a+3b)/(a+b)^2=(49-u^2)/4 and (3a^2+5ab+3b^2)/(a+b)^2=(11+u^2)/4. Thus the numerator is 539+38u^2-u^4, strictly increasing in u^2 on [0,1). Precisely the equal-radius pairs minimize, with angle free; the supremum is reached only in the limit min(a,b)/max(a,b)→0. No coplanar isotropic value is asserted. This is an analytic check; packaged check.py was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: This classifies a canonical affine invariant of a full elementary nonpolyhedral family, not an isolated integral. In particular it identifies the unique balance optimum, an exact stability deficit, and the sharp degeneration limit in one formula; neither the known volume nor containment radii give those quantitative statements. The result is a usable exact benchmark for discotope isotropic geometry.
